articles.title: Nigeria Targets Fresh Investments as NUPRC Spotlights 22 Offshore Projects
articles.originalTitle: NUPRC Highlights 22 Offshore Projects As Nigeria Targets New Investments
articles.content:
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has spotlighted 22 major offshore projects as part of a strategic pipeline designed to spur fresh investments into Nigeria's upstream petroleum sector, according to a recent commission statement.

According to a statement from the NUPRC on Wednesday, the projects were presented at the Nigeria Investment Forum 2026 in New York by the Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, who was represented by the Executive Commissioner, Corporate Services and Administration, Dr Kelechi Onyekachi Ofoegbu.

The pipeline comprises 12 deepwater and 10 shallow-water developments, including Bonga Southwest, Aparo, Zaba Zaba, Owowo, Bosi and Egina South.

The Commission also highlighted recent capital commitments to projects including Bonga North, Obeta Gas Development, HIN Associated Gas Development and Iseni Gas Development.

According to the NUPRC, the Petroleum Industry Act 2021 has provided the foundation for reforms aimed at improving the regulatory framework and making upstream projects more predictable and bankable.

“Eyesan noted that the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 has provided the foundation for restructuring the industry’s regulatory architecture, while subsequent government and Commission-led reforms are aimed at improving the predictability and bankability of upstream projects.

“Particular emphasis was placed on incentives for non-associated gas and deepwater developments, as well as measures designed to shorten contracting cycles and provide greater certainty around project economics,” read part of the statement.

The NUPRC has approved 120 Field Development Plans since 2024, representing more than $57 billion in potential investment, reflecting a significant pipeline of projects moving through the regulatory process.

What You Should Know

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) is actively pushing to attract foreign and local investments by presenting 22 major offshore oil and gas projects—comprising 12 deepwater and 10 shallow-water developments—at the Nigeria Investment Forum 2026.

Backed by ongoing reforms and the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021, these efforts aim to make the country's energy sector more predictable, bankable, and attractive to investors.

  • Positive Impact: Increased investments in offshore oil and gas projects can significantly boost national revenue, create jobs, and improve energy infrastructure in the long run.
  • Potential Concerns: Delays in project execution or unfavorable global market conditions could stall projected capital inflows, impacting the expected economic growth benefits.
articles.summary: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission has showcased 22 major offshore projects at the Nigeria Investment Forum 2026 to attract fresh investments into the upstream petroleum sector.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Will Revolutionize Teaching Rather Than Replace Educators, Says Governor Mbah
articles.originalTitle: Mbah: AI Will Transform Teaching, Not Replace Teachers
articles.content:
Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has stated that artificial intelligence is set to transform the teaching profession instead of displacing educators, while calling on teachers to adopt emerging technologies as vital instruments for enhancing educational results.

Mbah said AI could help teachers personalise learning, prepare lessons, identify gaps in students’ knowledge and widen access to information, but could not replicate the human qualities required to educate and mentor children.

The governor spoke on Tuesday at the 59th National Conference of Delegates of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) in Enugu, held under the theme, “Deployment of Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Education Will Erode the Place of Teachers in the Classroom: Myth or Reality?”

He said resisting AI would be counterproductive, comparing its growing influence to the impact of the steam engine during the Industrial Revolution.

“AI can assist the teacher. It can personalise learning, support lesson preparation, identify learning gaps and expand access to knowledge.

“But it cannot replace the human qualities that make a teacher a teacher – the ability to inspire, to mentor, to understand a child’s individual circumstances, to build character and to kindle ambition.

“The future is therefore not teacher versus technology. The future is teacher with technology.”

Mbah called for safeguards to ensure AI is deployed ethically and responsibly in schools, identifying data protection, regulation, ethical standards and continuous teacher training as essential components of the transition.

He said teachers should not become victims of technological advancement but should be positioned as “principal beneficiaries and drivers” of the transformation.

According to the governor, adequate safeguards and capacity-building would help replace fears surrounding AI with informed confidence and responsible adoption.

Mbah also highlighted his administration’s investment in education, saying the state had recruited 6,850 teachers and other education personnel in the last 40 months to address manpower shortages and improve the student-teacher ratio.

He said education had received 33 per cent of Enugu State’s total budget across three budget cycles under his administration, which he said was above the 15 to 20 per cent benchmark recommended by UNESCO.

The governor also cited the establishment of fully equipped, technology-driven Smart Green Schools across the state’s 260 wards as part of efforts to prepare pupils for a technology-driven future.

He said the investments reflected the administration’s belief that a world-class education system could not be achieved without a well-equipped and motivated teaching workforce.

Mbah commended the NUT National Executive Council for convening the conference and praised Kebbi State Governor Mohammed Nasir Idris for his contributions to the teaching profession.

He also commended the Registrar of the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria, Dr Ronke Shoyombo, and her management team for their efforts to promote professionalism and restore dignity to the teaching profession.

What You Should Know

Governor Peter Mbah addressed the 59th National Conference of Delegates of the Nigeria Union of Teachers in Enugu, emphasizing that while AI can streamline lesson preparation, personalize learning, and bridge knowledge gaps, it cannot replicate the essential human traits of mentorship and inspiration.

  • Positive Impact: The integration of AI tools and the establishment of technology-driven Smart Green Schools aim to equip students for a modern, tech-forward future while empowering teachers with advanced resources.
  • Potential Concerns: The transition requires careful regulation, robust data protection, ethical standards, and continuous capacity-building to ensure teachers benefit from the technological shift rather than face professional displacement.
articles.summary: Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah has asserted that artificial intelligence will enhance teaching rather than replace educators, encouraging teachers to leverage new technologies to improve student learning outcomes.

articles.title: Former TV Anchor Crowned King of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom
articles.originalTitle: PHOTOS: Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom Crowns Former TV Anchor as King
articles.content:
Edward Rukidi Kijanangom, a former television news anchor, assumed the throne on Tuesday as the newly crowned king of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom. Citing Reuters, his coronation officially establishes him as the 13th monarch of the Batooro community, thereby resolving an ongoing succession crisis. Additionally, TVC News Online notes that Kijanangoma steps into the role succeeding the late King Oyo.

The new monarch took the new royal name Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I in a traditional ceremony that ​included the slaughter of a bull and the sprinkling of a hen's blood in Tooro's capital, Fort Portal.

It was also reported that as part of the coronation rituals, Nyabongo I walked to Karuziika Palace between ​midnight and 3 a.m. before taking part in a mock battle for the crown.

Guests at the coronation included President Yoweri Museveni.

Earlier, Charles Kayondo Kamurasi, the Omusuuga or head of the ​Babiito clan who had been wielding power since Oyo Nyimba's death, handed over authority to the new king in a church service at ​St. John's Cathedral.

“We have a big task to protect our culture, our traditions and customs and good conduct among our people,” Nyabongo I said in his ‌maiden speech, pledging to rally his subjects to protect the environment.

See photos from the coronation courtesy of X | Uganda Media Centre:

What You Should Know

The Tooro Kingdom in Uganda has officially crowned Edward Rukidi Kijanangom as its 13th monarch, bringing a definitive close to the succession dispute that followed the passing of the late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV. The traditional coronation ceremony involved sacred rites, including the slaughter of a bull and a mock battle in the capital of Fort Portal, culminating in the formal transfer of power.

  • Positive Impact: The peaceful transition and resolution of the succession dispute bring stability and renewed cultural leadership to the Batooro people, ensuring the preservation of their heritage and traditions.
  • Potential Concerns: The transition requires the new monarch to successfully navigate modern governance alongside traditional expectations while maintaining environmental and cultural unity among his subjects.
articles.summary: Edward Rukidi Kijanangom has been crowned as the 13th monarch of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom, successfully bringing an end to a local succession dispute.

articles.title: Gombe Federal High Court Nullifies APC Billiri/Balanga Reps Primary, Orders Fresh Election
articles.originalTitle: Court Voids APC Billiri/Balanga Reps Primary In Gombe, Orders Fresh Exercise
articles.content:
A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe State has invalidated the All Progressives Congress primary election that initially selected Ali Isa as the party candidate for the Billiri/Balanga Federal Constituency ahead of the 2027 polls.

Justice Ibrahim Eneabo ruled that a person seeking to contest for the ticket of a political party must have been a registered member of the party for at least 21 days before its primary election.

The court consequently ordered the APC to conduct a fresh primary election for the federal constituency within 30 days.

The ruling comes about a week after another court nullified the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) primary that produced former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, as the party’s governorship candidate in Gombe State.

The PDP has since conducted another primary, which again produced Pantami as its candidate.

The latest ruling involving the APC adds another legal development to the preparations for the 2027 elections in Gombe State, with the affected parties and candidates facing the implications of the court decisions.

The APC is expected to comply with the order for a fresh primary within the stipulated 30-day period.

What You Should Know

A federal court in Gombe State has cancelled the APC primary election for the Billiri/Balanga Federal Constituency because the candidate, Ali Isa, did not meet the mandatory requirement of being a registered party member for at least 21 days before the primary. The court has directed the party to conduct a brand new primary election within the next 30 days.

  • Positive Impact: This ruling strengthens internal party democracy and ensures that political parties strictly follow electoral guidelines and constitutional membership timelines.
  • Potential Concerns: The decision creates sudden political uncertainty, additional financial costs, and logistical stress for the APC and its members as they rush to organize a new primary within a tight 30-day window.
articles.summary: The Federal High Court in Gombe has nullified the APC primary election for the Billiri/Balanga Federal Constituency, ordering a fresh exercise within 30 days.

articles.title: JAMB Pushes 2021–2025 Admission Acceptance Deadline to November 30
articles.originalTitle: JAMB Extends 2021–2025 Admission Acceptance Deadline To November 30
articles.content:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has shifted the final date for applicants holding unaccepted admission offers spanning the 2021 through 2025 admission exercises to November 30, 2026.

The Board said the extension was approved following a temporary disruption of its Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), which was unavailable for about 96 hours.

JAMB had initially fixed September 30, 2026, as the deadline for affected candidates to accept or reject their outstanding admission offers.

It described the new November 30 deadline as the final extension, urging candidates to take immediate action rather than wait until the deadline.

Candidates who fail to accept or reject their outstanding offers by November 30 will no longer be able to do so under the current window.

JAMB said any subsequent request to update an admission record would attract the applicable penalty fee.

The Board said the extension was particularly important for candidates whose admission records were not reflected on the matriculation list, warning that this could affect their eligibility for certain benefits, including participation in the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme.

Candidates who accept their outstanding offers will be able to print their admission letters, while those who reject them will have their status reverted to “Not Admitted” on their CAPS dashboards.

JAMB said the process would enable it to update its records and ensure that the national admission database accurately reflects candidates’ current admission status.

The Board also clarified that candidates who are no longer studying at institutions where they were previously offered admission, or who have changed programmes, may accept the outstanding offers and subsequently apply for the appropriate correction or deletion of the previous admission where necessary.

Candidates currently pursuing a second degree but holding unaccepted admission offers from previous years may also reject those offers without affecting their ongoing studies.

JAMB further assured candidates who have received admission offers for the 2026 academic session but still have outstanding offers from previous years that rejecting the earlier offers would not affect their current admission.

According to the Board, all outstanding offers from the 2021 to 2025 admission exercises that remain neither accepted nor rejected by November 30 will automatically revert to “Not Admitted” in its records.

JAMB therefore urged all affected candidates to use the extension to regularise their admission records before the final deadline.

What You Should Know

JAMB has given students with pending admission offers from previous years more time to sort out their school placements. This extension comes after the central system experienced a temporary downtime, making it difficult for candidates to access their dashboards.

  • Positive Impact: Affected candidates get a crucial second chance to secure their admission status, print their admission letters, and clear any obstacles preventing them from participating in the NYSC scheme.
  • Potential Concerns: Failing to act before the final November 30 deadline means offers will automatically change to "Not Admitted," and fixing records later will attract extra penalty fees.
articles.summary: The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board has extended the deadline for candidates to accept or reject outstanding admission offers from the 2021 to 2025 academic sessions to November 30, following a brief system disruption.

articles.title: National Assembly Directs Security Forces to Prioritize Rescue of Abducted Nigerians Amid Mounting Insecurity
articles.content:
The National Assembly yesterday directed security agencies to intensify their operations aimed at rescuing Nigerians held captive by armed groups across the country, expressing deep concern over the persistent security challenges facing rural communities.

The call came on the floor of the Senate and House of Representatives at resumed plenary on Tuesday, after a 68-day annual recess. Both chambers subsequently adjourned plenary until October 13, citing ongoing rehabilitation work in the Senate and House chambers.

In his speech titled “Keeping Faith with Nigeria” to set the legislative agenda, Senate President Godswill Akpabio referenced recent abductions during Friday prayer in Marisa Local Government Area of Niger State and other parts of the nation, declaring that the parliament cannot consider itself free while citizens remain in captivity.

“So long as a single Nigerian languishes in captivity, a part of Nigeria is held captive and this Chamber cannot call itself free of the burden. We call upon our security agencies to pursue the rescue of captives and the protection of vulnerable communities with renewed vigour,” Akpabio stated.

On its part, the House of Representatives called for coordinated security operations to secure the immediate and safe release of 116 schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa in Askira Uba Local Government Area of Borno State, and other parts of the country.

The call followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by the member representing Askira-Uba/Hawul Federal Constituency, Midala Balami.

Balami said the continued captivity had subjected the victims’ families and affected communities to “unbearable emotional distress, uncertainty and fear,” demanding urgent and decisive action to secure their release.

Security analysts observe that the lawmakers’ nudge amounts to “mere rhetoric” unless it is backed by concrete action.

Daily Trust reports that the appeal is coming on the back of the prolonged stay of hundreds of victims in captivity.

Akpabio, who also spoke on flood disaster, economic hardship and electioneering ahead of the 2027 general elections, pledged that the Senate would deploy its powers of legislation, appropriation, and oversight to support security institutions and safeguard lives and property.

Highlighting the recent flooding that destroyed homes and farmlands during the recess, he called on all levels of government to expedite emergency response and relief measures to prevent food shortages and support affected families.

On the national economy, the Senate President urged lawmakers to ensure policy discussions reflect the everyday struggles of citizens coping with the high cost of living, including small business owners, job-seeking graduates and households.

He reiterated the Senate’s renewed commitment to addressing the pressing national challenges confronting citizens, including the rising cost of living, widespread insecurity, and severe flooding across the country.

“Many Nigerians continue to bear a very heavy cost of living,” Akpabio said, stressing the importance of carefully examining ongoing economic reforms.

“The sittings of the Senate ceased in plenary for a season, but the life of Nigeria did not cease. Our victories should be measured in safer communities, better livelihoods for all Nigerians, and a stronger country for those we serve and for generations unborn,” he added.

With political activities intensifying ahead of the 2027 general elections, Akpabio cautioned political actors against divisive rhetoric, religious profiling, and electoral violence.

“We must reject violence and intimidation, and resist the falsehoods that travel swiftly and leave distrust in their wake. No electoral prize is worth a Nigerian life,” he said.

Akpabio assured the public that lawmaking would not yield to political campaigns, noting that senators would remain at their posts throughout the electioneering period.

He also noted that as Nigeria marks its 66th Independence Anniversary on October 1, public officers must uphold patriotism and steadfastness in addressing national challenges.

Over 800 abducted in 3 months

The country has witnessed several cases of abductions, with more than 800 people kidnapped in the last three months, according to several media reports.

At least 18 residents, including eight women, were kidnapped on September 25, along the Adoka-Ankpa road at the Benue/Kogi border while travelling to Kogi State for a burial.

In Niger State, 47 farmers were abducted while harvesting groundnuts in Rimi, an agricultural community in the Mariga area of Niger State. The incident happened on Sunday, September 27. Most of the victims were women.

Niger State Police Spokesperson, SP Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the incident, saying that over 20 people were kidnapped.

“On 28th Sept 2026, a report indicated that on 27th Sept 2026 at about 3 pm, suspected bandits abducted over twenty persons at Mukura village, Kasuwan-Garba District of Mariga LGA. Joint security rescue efforts are ongoing,” he said.

More than 50 people were abducted and about 10 vehicles set ablaze on Sunday and in the early hours of Monday when bandits attacked Bungudu, Yargada, Maikogo and Magama Mairake communities in Bungudu, Gusau and Maru LGAs, Zamfara State.

A survivor, Malam Lawali Kutsa Ada, said the attackers stormed Magama Mairake around midnight, shooting sporadically before conducting house-to-house searches.

He said the bandits abducted about 44 people, mostly women and children, and took them into the bush.

Kutsa said the attackers also set about 10 vehicles, including Canter trucks and other commercial vehicles, on fire.

Another resident said police responded to a distress call but could not immediately confront the attackers because of their numbers and superior weapons.

The attackers also invaded Yargada and Maikogo, where an unspecified number of people were abducted. In Bungudu, the bandits reportedly killed several people and abducted 11 others.

The police spokesman, DSP Yazid Abubakar, confirmed the abduction of 11 people in Bungudu, saying a search-and-rescue team had been deployed.

He said the command was still investigating the actual number of victims in the affected communities.

On Saturday, a newly married couple, identified as Funmilayo Bamidele and Rev. Abiodun David, were abducted by armed assailants while returning from their engagement ceremony in Eruku, Kwara State.

They were reportedly travelling with four other passengers when their vehicle was intercepted along the Iyemero–Eruku route bordering Kogi and Kwara states.

On August 21, 2026, terrorists attacked Dekara, Kpenya, Sabon-Gida and Gidan-Zana communities in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State while worshippers were observing Juma’at prayers.

Two days later, the terrorists released a video claiming to have abducted 500 worshippers, including women and children. Families later authenticated the video after identifying their relatives in the clip.

The affected communities subsequently released the names of 547 worshippers allegedly abducted during the attacks, contradicting the claim by Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago that 63 people were seized.

In the document, the Youth President of Dekara District, Zubairu Umar, said 547 community members were taken into the Kainji Lake National Park forest. He said their whereabouts and condition remained unknown.

In May, insurgents attacked schools in Mussa, Askira-Uba LGA of Borno State, abducting 42 pupils.

On 29 June, gunmen attacked Government Day Secondary School in Lassa while students were taking examinations and abducted at least 36 students. The two incidents left 78 children in captivity.

Parents of the abducted schoolchildren have staged several protests in Borno to call the government’s attention to their plight, alleging that they have been abandoned.

On Monday, the Chairman of the Abducted Children’s Parents Association, Ishaku Suya, told Daily Trust that they are taking their protest to Abuja after the federal government failed to respond to their six-day ultimatum to rescue their children.

The parents said they would storm the Presidential Villa to demand the intervention of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and would remain in Abuja until they were granted an audience with the President.

The children have spent more than 100 days in captivity.

Bandits demand N94m, woman gives birth in captivity

Meanwhile, bandits have demanded N94 million ransom from families of the 47 farmers abducted from Mariga LGA of Niger State.

The kidnappers had on Saturday abducted 47 farmers, mostly women harvesting groundnuts on their farms at Tugan-Rimi.

The Chairman of Mariga LGA, Aliyu Bagga Muhammadu, who confirmed the incident, said the bandits had contacted the families of the victims, demanding N2 million for each captive.

“My local government is faced with a serious security challenge. The information at my disposal indicates that women were harvesting groundnuts on their farm when bandits invaded the area and assembled them and took them away.

“They also saw some men working on their farms and took them away. But women formed the majority of those kidnapped. One of the women had given birth in captivity,” he said.

According to Muhammadu, security operatives have been mobilised to go after the abductors and ensure the safe release of the victims.

He noted that the joint security operatives had earlier engaged the kidnappers around Kasuwan Garba and Beri axes, during which one of the vigilantes sustained injuries.

It was further revealed that the armed men were reportedly seen moving through areas between Mangoro and Wamba after allegedly emerging from the Dogon Dawa axis.

The Spokesperson for the Niger State Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, confirmed the incident, saying that over 20 people were kidnapped.

Women protest abduction of 18 residents in Benue

Women from Tyomu community in Makurdi LGA of Benue State on Tuesday protested the abduction of 18 residents, including eight women, kidnapped along the Adoka-Ankpa road while travelling to Kogi State for a burial.

Our correspondent reports that the protesters blocked the Makurdi-Gboko road at Tyomu, Fidi Council Ward, demanding government intervention to secure the release of the victims, who were reportedly abducted by gunmen on Friday evening shortly after Adoka along the Benue/Kogi boundary.

The protesters said the victims, who were travelling in a bus to attend a burial, had remained in captivity despite efforts to raise money demanded by their abductors.

They said that the kidnappers demanded N30 million ransom, while residents reportedly raised and paid N3 million, but the victims were yet to be released.

The protesters who blocked the roads for several hours demanded that government officials come to the area and address them before they would reopen the road.

It was gathered that the Chairman of Makurdi LGA, Joseph Keffi, in company with other government officials, later arrived at the scene and assured the community that the council would collaborate with security agencies to secure the safe return of the abducted residents.

The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) in the state, Peter Aondongu, told our correspondent that the command did not receive any formal report about the kidnapping, but said its operatives on patrol along the route at the weekend sighted an abandoned vehicle and suspected that occupants might have been taken away.

He said the police could not confirm the number of victims abducted until the details of the incident are made available to the command.

Aondongu, who said the police later cleared the road, appealed to the protesting community for patience while security operatives made efforts to rescue the victims.

The Special Adviser to the state governor on Internal Security, Chief Joseph Har, told journalists in Makurdi on Tuesday evening that the government had reported the incident to relevant security agencies, adding that efforts were underway to locate the victims and secure their release.

Har said the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Adoka and security personnel in surrounding areas were working to rescue the victims.

He, however, explained that the operation was being handled cautiously in order not to expose the victims to harm or result in collateral damage.

Har said the government was keeping the victims’ families informed about developments, including the progress of efforts to rescue their relatives.

He also expressed concern over travelling to Kogi State at night, particularly along routes known to be vulnerable to attacks, saying residents should avoid exposing themselves to unnecessary risks.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said the victims, who were from Tyomu community, had hired Ejifa Travel Services to convey them to and from a burial ceremony in Kogi State.

Iorpev said the travellers were kidnapped around Ankpa, adding that the transport company allegedly failed to immediately report the incident to the police.

‘Senate’s call without action is rhetoric’

A security and public affairs commentator, Babayo Sule, an Associate Professor, described the Senate’s call as rhetoric unless backed by concrete action.

Sule said similar directives had been issued to security chiefs in the past without producing the desired results, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged insecurity.

“In my own view, I see this call by the Senate as mere political rhetoric because this is not the first, second or third time the security chiefs would be directed to relocate to such places or to bring an end to the dilemma of security challenges, but all of them do not yield any required results,” he said.

He recalled that there had been presidential directives for security chiefs and service commanders to relocate to flashpoints and remain there until security was restored, but said such orders had often failed to produce lasting results.

“Sometimes, they might either relocate for a few days and then return to their comfort zones in Abuja or elsewhere, or they may not be relocated at all and the challenges continue as they are,” Sule stated.

He said the government needed to demonstrate the political will to tackle insecurity by addressing the operational challenges confronting security personnel.

“The best approach that can be done is simply to exhibit and demonstrate serious will and the desire to do it by looking at it squarely in terms of the financial need, the logistics, the weapons, the information, the intelligence and the free hand that the security personnel need,” he said.

Sule also stressed the need for collaboration between security agencies and communities affected by insecurity, saying local communities could play an important role in providing intelligence and supporting security operations.

He further cautioned against relying on official pronouncements without corresponding action, arguing that the effectiveness of the Senate’s directive should ultimately be measured by tangible results on the ground.

“Otherwise, it will just continue to be a political gimmick, particularly as elections are forthcoming. People should not be hoodwinked or just be subjected to a deception of such a statement. Let there be action and not just a mere statement or just a mere viable intention which does not translate into action,” Sule said.

What You Should Know

The National Assembly has resumed from its annual recess with a strong demand for security forces to step up efforts in rescuing hundreds of citizens currently held captive by criminal gangs across various parts of the country. Lawmakers from both the Senate and the House of Representatives highlighted ongoing mass abductions—including schoolchildren in Borno State, farmers in Niger State, and travelers in Benue and Kwara—as a heavy burden on the nation's conscience. While the legislative appeal underscores government awareness of the crisis, security analysts note that such directives must be backed by concrete logistical support and political will to yield real results.

  • Positive Impact: Heightened parliamentary attention could compel security agencies to deploy more resources and coordinate better rescue operations for vulnerable communities and abducted individuals.
  • Potential Concerns: Without practical operational backing, increased funding, and improved intelligence, legislative calls risk remaining mere rhetoric, leaving citizens continuously exposed to violent attacks and economic disruption in farming belts.
articles.summary: The National Assembly has urged security agencies to ramp up rescue operations for captives held by armed groups, as lawmakers express deep concern over worsening rural insecurity.

articles.title: National Assembly Extends 2025 Capital Budget Implementation Deadline Again
articles.content:
Lawmakers at the National Assembly on Tuesday pushed the implementation cutoff date for the capital projects outlined in the 2025 Appropriation Act from September 30 to December 31, 2026.

This marks the fourth time lawmakers have prolonged the lifespan of the 2025 capital budget.

At the Senate, the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, said the extension was necessary to provide ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) with sufficient time to complete capital projects for which funds had already been appropriated and released.

According to him, several factors, including procurement procedures, contract execution, mobilisation, certification of completed works and payment processes, could affect the timely implementation of capital projects.

He said the amendment would provide “the necessary legal and administrative window” required for the completion of ongoing projects.

Bamidele warned that allowing the existing deadline to expire without an extension could create administrative and legal difficulties for MDAs while increasing the possibility of projects being abandoned or left incomplete.

He also dismissed concerns that the extension could weaken accountability or legislative oversight, insisting that the measure remained subject to existing fiscal and legislative controls.

The Deputy Senate President, Senator Barau Jibrin, backed the extension, describing it as an important measure to prevent the proliferation of abandoned projects across the country.

The Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, also supported the extension but cautioned his colleagues against turning the debate into an avenue for political blame.

The House of Representatives also extended the implementation of the capital component of the 2025 Appropriation Act for the fourth time, moving the deadline from September 30 to December 31, 2026.

The extension was approved during Tuesday’s plenary following a motion moved by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere.

Leading debate on the bill, the House Leader said several factors affecting the Nigerian economy had made it difficult to complete implementation of the capital component of the 2025 budget within the existing timeframe.

He said the extension was necessary to provide adequate time for the implementation of the projects and programmes captured under the capital component of the budget.

Timeline for extensions

Daily Trust reports that the National Assembly first extended the implementation period in December 2025, moving the deadline to March 31, 2026.

The fourth extension comes a day before the expiration of the latest deadline.

With Tuesday’s decision, Ministries, Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government will have an additional three months to implement projects and utilise funds appropriated under the 2025 capital budget.

The repeated extensions have allowed the implementation of the 2025 capital budget to continue alongside the 2026 budget.

Extending 2025 budget shows gross fiscal indiscipline – Expert

Economist Dr. Marcel Okeke has described the budget extension as a “gross fiscal indiscipline,” warning that such a practice distorts the purpose of annual appropriation laws and weakens public accountability.

Okeke said while the decision to ensure that capital expenditure contained in the budget is eventually implemented might appear, on the surface, to demonstrate a determination to complete government projects, carrying budgetary provisions from one year into another raises serious fiscal and governance concerns.

According to him, an Appropriation Act is a law designed to govern government spending within a specified financial year.

He argued that repeatedly altering the timing of budget implementation or moving portions of an appropriation from one year to another amounts to a distortion of the law, particularly because each Appropriation Act is intended to cover a one-year period.

The economist also expressed concern that carrying projects and allocations from previous budgets into subsequent years could make effective monitoring more difficult especially as the nation is in an election year.

He explained that projects approved and budgeted for a particular year are expected to be monitored within the framework of that year's budget.

When such projects are repeatedly carried forward, he said, they may not receive the level of monitoring and scrutiny ordinarily expected under the current appropriation.

Okeke further lamented what he described as inadequate public reporting on budget implementation. He recalled that in previous administrations, finance officials regularly provided detailed budget breakdowns and periodic updates on implementation.

He questioned the absence of regular quarterly or half-yearly updates on the execution of the budget, saying greater transparency would enable citizens and other stakeholders to assess government performance.

Lawyers raise legal, accountability concerns over 2025 budget extension

A human rights lawyer, Udochukwu Onoh, said the recurring extensions reflected a wider problem with Nigeria’s budget process, particularly delays in passing and assenting to appropriation bills.

“Every budget is intended to be expended within the same year. Unfortunately, in Nigeria, it takes us longer to deliberate on budget approval and presidential assent,” Onoh said.

Onoh also raised concerns over the treatment of unspent appropriations, stressing that government agencies should properly account for funds before another budget cycle takes effect.

According to him, where implementation of a budget extends into another fiscal year, the relevant agencies must ensure that all expenditure is properly retired and accounted for.

Another lawyer, Victoria Adaji, described the repeated extension of the 2025 capital budget as a significant challenge to Nigeria’s public finance management framework.

She said the legal implications became more pronounced where the extended 2025 capital budget operates alongside an already signed 2026 Appropriation Act and preparations for the 2027 fiscal year.

“The legal implications of the National Assembly extending the 2025 budget’s capital component for a fourth time to December 31, 2026, while overlapping with a signed 2026 budget and staring down 2027 fiscal discussions, represent a structural breakdown in Nigeria’s public finance management,” Adaji said.

The Country Director of Accountability Lab Nigeria, Friday Odeh, also criticised the fourth extension, saying it could weaken the legal force of the Appropriation Act and make public expenditure more difficult to monitor.

He also argued that repeated extensions could conceal deeper problems in revenue generation and the ability of government agencies to execute capital projects.

“Repeated extensions disguise chronic revenue deficits and poor capital absorptive capacity as mere procurement delays,” he said.

Odeh further alleged that continually extending implementation timelines could affect cash-flow management and borrowing requirements, with potential consequences for inflation.

He also criticised the National Assembly’s handling of the extensions, arguing that lawmakers should use their constitutional oversight powers to enforce greater fiscal discipline.

He proposed measures to strengthen accountability, including project-level audits of items covered by the extension and stricter conditions for future extensions.

What You Should Know

The National Assembly has prolonged the lifespan of the 2025 capital budget for the fourth time, giving ministries and government agencies until the end of 2026 to finish ongoing projects. While lawmakers argue this prevents abandoned projects and grants sufficient execution time, economic experts and legal practitioners have criticized the move as fiscal indiscipline that complicates public financial management.

  • Positive Impact: The extension prevents government projects from being abandoned midway, ensuring that funds already released are properly utilized to complete vital infrastructure across the country.
  • Potential Concerns: Critics warn that overlapping budget cycles create transparency challenges, weaken legislative oversight, and make it difficult to monitor public spending properly.
articles.summary: The National Assembly has extended the implementation deadline for the capital component of the 2025 Appropriation Act for the fourth consecutive time.

articles.title: Tragedy Strikes As Three Die In Stampede At Niger State Government House
articles.originalTitle: 3 killed in stampede at Niger govt house
articles.content:
At least three individuals have tragically lost their lives, with several others sustaining injuries, following a chaotic stampede at the Niger State Government House located in Minna.

The injured victims are currently receiving treatment at the Minna General Hospital.

It was gathered that the incident occurred on Tuesday night when youths reportedly linked to a planned protest over the recent deaths of 37 artisanal miners were allegedly invited to the Government House to shelve their protest.

Among those who lost their lives were a woman, Dije, and her daughter, Hurairat, both internally displaced persons (IDPs) from Allawa community in Shiroro Local Government Area.

Hurairat’s husband, Abubakar, a butcher, was reportedly killed by bandits in 2023 along the Allawa-Pandogari Road.

Following the attack and the subsequent desertion of the Allawa community, Hurairat had been living in Minna as an IDP.

Dije, who was staying with her husband as an IDP in Gurmana, had visited her daughter, Hurairat, when they both heard that the governor was going to distribute money at the Government House. They subsequently went there.

Mallam Musa Allawa, one of the IDPs, told Daily Trust that Dije and Hurairat would both be buried at 10am on Wednesday.

Sources, including some appointees of the governor, had posted on social media before the stampede that the youths had gathered at the Government House to show solidarity with Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago.

One of the appointees told Daily Trust that other people, including women, later trooped to the Government House after hearing that the governor would distribute N10,000 to those gathered.

When contacted, the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Bologi Ibrahim, said the government would release a statement in due course.

Also, the Spokesperson for the Niger Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, promised to verify the information and revert.

What You Should Know

A deadly stampede occurred at the Niger State Government House in Minna following reports of a cash distribution, resulting in the deaths of three people, including an internally displaced woman and her daughter.

  • Positive Impact: Highlights the urgent need for government transparency, organized crowd control, and improved welfare delivery systems to prevent future tragedies during public events.
  • Potential Concerns: Exposes the vulnerabilities of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and raises serious security concerns regarding the management of large crowds drawn by financial palliative distributions.
articles.summary: A tragic stampede at the Niger State Government House in Minna has claimed three lives and left several others injured.

articles.title: Sokoto State Government Vows to Assist 16-Year-Old Orphan Who Excelled in JAMB with 353 Score
articles.originalTitle: Sokoto govt to support orphan who scored 353 in JAMB
articles.content:
The Sokoto State Government has initiated efforts to provide assistance to Muhammad Sirajo Abubakar, a 16-year-old orphan who recorded an impressive score of 353 in the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).

According to a statement on Wednesday by the Public Relations Officer of the Ministry of Higher Education, Ibrahim Iya, the move followed his outstanding performance in the examination and public attention generated by his story.

Muhammad, who lost both parents at a young age, scored 92 in Mathematics, 67 in English, 98 in Physics and 96 in Chemistry in the 2026 JAMB examination.

His WAEC result also showed three As, four Bs and one C, while his Biology result is still awaited.

The student is seeking admission to study Mechatronics Engineering at Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria.

According to the statement, the Commissioner for Higher Education, Prof Isa Muhammad Maishanu, contacted the state JAMB Coordinator, Ibrahim Muazu Hassan, after coming across Muhammad’s story online.

The commissioner directed the coordinator to reach out to the student and facilitate his visit to the ministry for possible intervention.

Muhammad was subsequently brought to the Ministry of Higher Education on Tuesday, where he was received by the commissioner and officials of the ministry.

Maishanu commended the student for his academic performance, courage and commitment to education despite losing his parents at a young age.

He said the ministry would examine Muhammad’s situation and work towards providing the appropriate support to enable him continue his education.

The intervention, the statement said, was in line with the education priorities of Governor Ahmad Aliyu’s administration under its nine-point Smart Agenda.

It added that the government would explore necessary support to facilitate Muhammad’s educational journey and enable him pursue his ambition of becoming a Mechatronics Engineer.

The ministry also commended the state JAMB coordinator for his prompt response and assistance in bringing the student to the ministry.

What You Should Know

This news highlights how exceptional academic performance can attract government attention and create life-changing opportunities for underprivileged students in Nigeria.

  • Positive Impact: It offers hope, financial relief, and educational backing to a brilliant orphan, helping him pursue his dream of studying Mechatronics Engineering at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria.
  • Potential Support: It reflects a positive commitment by the Sokoto State administration under Governor Ahmad Aliyu to prioritize education and reward academic excellence among young citizens.
articles.summary: The Sokoto State Government has stepped in to support 16-year-old orphan Muhammad Sirajo Abubakar, who achieved an outstanding score of 353 in the 2026 UTME.

articles.title: Kano Police Smash Motorcycle Theft Syndicate, Recover Six Bikes and Arrest Eight
articles.originalTitle: Police bust motorcycle theft syndicate, recover 6 motorcycles
articles.content:
Operatives of the Kano State Police Command have apprehended eight individuals on allegations of motorcycle theft, successfully retrieving six stolen motorcycles in the process.

The command said the suspects were arrested following a report of criminal conspiracy, theft and receiving stolen property involving a Bajaj Boxer motorcycle at Sabon Gari Police Division on September 22.

According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, two suspects, Maharazu Mohammed, 22, and Hassan Abdullahi, 22, both of PRP Quarters, Kano, were initially arrested.

He said their confessions led to the arrest of six other suspects, bringing the number of those arrested to eight.

Police recovered six motorcycles comprising two Motor B, three Haojue and one Companion motorcycle.

The command also handed over three previously recovered vehicles to their owners after verification and documentation.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, said investigation is ongoing to recover more stolen motorcycles and arrest other members of the alleged syndicate.

The command urged members of the public whose motorcycles were stolen to contact the police for identification and possible recovery, with proof of ownership.

Police said the suspects would be charged to court after completion of investigation.

What You Should Know

The Kano State Police Command has successfully dismantled a motorcycle theft syndicate, arresting eight suspects and recovering six stolen motorcycles following an initial tip-off at the Sabon Gari Police Division.

This operation also led to the return of three previously recovered vehicles to their rightful owners after careful verification, while police efforts continue to round up remaining gang members and trace more stolen properties.

  • Positive Impact: Enhanced security for motorcycle owners in Kano, leading to the recovery of stolen property and justice for victims who can reclaim their assets with proof of ownership.
  • Potential Concerns: The prevalence of organized theft syndicates targeting everyday commuters and commercial riders underscores ongoing security challenges that require continuous vigilance from vehicle owners.
articles.summary: The Kano State Police Command has arrested eight suspects in connection with a motorcycle theft ring and successfully recovered six stolen motorcycles.
